item.title: Namibia create history with Ireland ODI series triumph
item.description:
Namibia created history on Sunday when they won their first bilateral ODI series against a Full Member when they defeated Ireland by five wickets in Windhoek.
The victory sealed a 3-2 result for Namibia in the five-match ODI series on home soil and bodes well for the side ahead of next year's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup they will co-host with South Africa and Zimbabwe.
Pacers JJ Smith and Jack Brassell shared seven wickets to help skittle Ireland for just 129 and decent hands from opener Louren Steenkamp (42) and skipper Gerhard Erasmus (30) ensured a simple run chase and an impressive series triumph.
Erasmus was named Player of the Series for his 263 runs and four wickets across the five matches, while Smith was adjudged Player of the Match in the series finale after collecting the economical figures of 4/20 from nine overs.
Only four Ireland players scored in double figures in the series finale and skipper Lorcan Tucker was bitterly disappointed with the efforts of his players.
"Obviously, it was a disappointing day for us," Tucker said.
"We came here today excited about the opportunities with the series on the line, but I don't think we quite rocked up from a skills perspective.
"We have learned a lot, but I think we've a lot to reflect on going forward.
"Credit to Namibia, they played diligent cricket and did that for longer periods of time than us - that's why they won the series today."
Ireland have already booked their place at next year's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier courtesy of their spot on the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings, while Namibia will likely have to earn their position via the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off.
Series schedule:
First ODI: Windhoek, Ireland won by 55 runs
Second ODI: Windhoek, Namibia won by 31 runs
Third ODI: Windhoek, Namibia won by 63 runs
Fourth ODI: Windhoek, Ireland won by 130 runs
Fifth ODI: Windhoek, Namibia won by five wickets

item.title: Messi sends Miami second with 2-1 win at New England
item.description:
Lionel Messi's late strike catapulted Inter Miami above New England and into second place with a tense 2-1 comeback victory over their MLS Eastern Conference rivals Sunday.
Messi's typically crafty effort after scurrying through three defenders in the 83rd minute was enough to secure three points, with an own goal by his teammate Ian Fray four minutes later ruled out for a marginal offside.
The 39-year-old Argentine superstar also provided an improvised assist off the back of his head for German Berterame, after Daniel Gazdag had put New England in front early in the second half.
Victory sent Miami a point clear of the New England Revolution with one game left, meaning a win against Charlotte on Saturday will guarantee home advantage until the Conference Finals.
It also secured Miami's spot in next year's CONCACAF Champions Cup.
"It was such an important occasion...they're a very tough team -- really difficult -- so I think it was a tremendous effort," said Berterame.
After a goalless first half, New England's Peyton Miller slipped down the right flank to the byline in the 53rd minute. His cut-back pass was backheeled by Ilay Feingold to Gazdag, who smashed the ball home.
Miami came close to equalizing soon after the hour, as Berterame followed up on a Messi effort saved by Matt Turner, only to have his shot cleared off the line by Brooklyn Raines.
In the 69th minute, Telasco Segovia flicked a ball high into the box toward Messi, who was racing forward between two defenders but somehow headed it blindly off the back of his head to Berterame, who scored.
Messi got on the scoresheet himself in the 83rd minute, collecting the ball just outside the D, spinning and skipping past three tackles before wrapping his left foot around the ball and sending it low into the far corner past US national team goalkeeper Turner.
New England thought they had been gifted an equalizer with three minutes remaining.
Fray inexplicably headed a hopeful Luca Langoni cross into his own net despite no pressure, but the New England substitute was ruled offside on video review.
The Eastern Conference's final playoff berths were also determined Sunday.
Columbus Crew and Orlando City both qualified after 10th-placed New York Red Bulls lost 3-2 to runaway leaders Nashville.
Sam Sturridge's stoppage-time strike sealed a comeback victory from 2-0 down for Nashville, who have tied the record for the most points in MLS history, on 74, with a game still to play.
Nashville lifted the Supporters' Shield trophy on Sunday at their Geodis Park stadium, where they have not lost all year, becoming the first team in MLS history with 15 home wins.
Higher seeds retain home advantage through the post-season until the MLS Cup, which will take place on December 18.

item.title: Antonelli becomes youngest Formula One world champion
item.description:
Kimi Antonelli drove the perfect race to finish third in his Mercedes at the Mexico Grand Prix and seal his place in Formula One history as the youngest world champion.
Max Verstappen took the chequered flag but all eyes were on the young Italian who takes the crown at the age of 20 years and 68 days, more than three years younger than Sebastian Vettel in 2010.
He is the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
"We did it. I wouldn't be here without Mercedes, without my family," said an emotional Antonelli who has won nine races so far this season.
"I am very grateful for this moment, it will be with me forever. I am speechless, just trying to process what happened.
"It's been an incredible season and to share this podium with Max and Lewis (Hamilton) is incredible. I am looking forward to some more battles in the future."
The race broke into two parts as it was suspended after 46 of the 71 laps following a crash involving Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas.
The Finn's suspension on the front left side had collapsed causing his wheel to buckle and making him a helpless passenger as his car flew backwards off the track and slammed into the barriers.
The 37-year-old Bottas was slow to emerge from his car but waved to the crowd as he walked away, with all the other cars returning to the pits to await a restart.
Antonelli, who needed just to finish in the top nine to seal the title, was running third in his Mercedes when the race was stopped behind Red Bull's Verstappen and the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc.
His nearest challenger teammate George Russell was out of the running after suffering a poor start dropping from second on the grid to fifth and struggling with his power.
Russell had to win to have any hope of prolonging the title race.
Lewis Hamilton, who started on pole and also needed to win to push Antonelli, was furious with his Ferrari teammate after an incident at the start that saw Leclerc leave the track and steal the lead. The Monegasque was handed a five-second penalty but he retained track superiority over Hamilton.
That changed on the restart when Hamilton powered past Antonelli and Leclerc and bumped wheels with Verstappen before settling into second.
There was a further yellow flag when the Racing Bull of Arvid Lindblad also crashed out 10 laps from the end after tangling with the McLaren of Oscar Piastri.
Antonelli sat tight in third as Hamilton continued to press Verstappen. It was entirely appropriate that the young Italian, in tears as he crossed the line, was led in by two of the all-time great drivers with 11 championships between them.

item.title: Mbappe strikes after China controversy as Real beat Santander
item.description:
Kylian Mbappe moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.
The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d'Or to Bayern Munich's Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.
Real Madrid's match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.
Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande were also on target to keep third-place Madrid within three points of leaders Barcelona, who thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday.
Jose Mourinho's side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind city rivals Atletico Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.
"In the first half we were very strong, we came out to play well," Mourinho told reporters.
"The team is growing, playing well, I think we should have scored even more goals with the chances we had."
Mbappe won a soft penalty as he went down under little pressure from Matteo Prati, smashing it home to put Madrid ahead at the Sardinero stadium in the 11th minute.
It was the 27-year-old's 12th league goal of the season, trailing only Barcelona's Raphinha with 15 in the scoring charts.
Madrid had control of the game and a fine pass from Arda Guler sent Bellingham through on goal for the second.
The England international knocked the ball past the goalkeeper and rolled home for his 50th goal since joining Madrid in 2023.
"Reaching 50 goals with Real Madrid is very special," Bellingham told Real Madrid TV.
"We played very well. It was very important to win after the victory at Camp Nou (against Barca last weekend), so we are very happy."
Guler spurned a good opportunity for the third after being set up by Mbappe, before Madrid's record signing Diomande lashed home from the edge of the box.
The hosts started the second half well, pushing Madrid back, much to the chagrin of Mourinho, who yelled at his players.
Madrid regained their control and racked up several more chances, with Mbappe hitting the post and Bellingham denied by Racing goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala.
Racing won a penalty after Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni handled in the box, but the award was cancelled after a VAR review.
Bellingham had a second goal ruled out in stoppage time after he strayed offside before finding the net and Endrick bent an effort narrowly wide from distance.
Hosts Racing, 16th, back in La Liga for the first time in 14 seasons, fell to their first home defeat of the campaign.
Earlier Sevilla, sixth, suffered a 3-1 loss at Getafe, who moved into mid-table.
"(Madrid's penalty award) annoys me," Racing coach Jose Alberto told DAZN.
"Evidently we came across a great Madrid, who put us under a lot of pressure in the first half hour, and were much better than us, but what conditions everything was the first goal and the penalty."
Valencia, 19th, beat Elche 1-0 with a well-taken goal from Umar Sadiq to move to within a point of safety after a bad start to the season.
Elsewhere Athletic Bilbao, seventh, edged fifth-place Real Sociedad 2-1 in an entertaining Basque derby clash at San Mames stadium.
Inaki Williams lobbed Athletic ahead early on before Luka Sucic drilled home from the edge of the box to level.
Alex Berenguer controversially restored Athletic's advantage just before half-time from the penalty spot, after Jon Aramburu was adjudged to have fouled Nico Williams, although he appeared to win the ball.
"I think it's incredible that a penalty like that is given when I touched the ball, even Nico said it," complained Aramburu to DAZN.
Spanish World Cup-winning goalkeeper Unai Simon made several fine saves to ensure Los Leones claimed the three points.

item.title: The chars have no legal memory
item.description:
Bangladesh has a master plan for its haors . It has a distinctive legal and institutional framework for the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
But after more than two decades of working among the chars of the northern riverine areas, watching homes disappear into the river and reappear somewhere else, I still struggle to answer a simple question: Who is responsible for people who live on land that does not stay?
I have travelled for years through the char areas of Kurigram and Gaibandha, along the Jamuna and Brahmaputra.
I have watched families dismantle their homes for the third or fourth time in a decade -- tin sheets pulled down, bamboo bundled, chickens loaded onto boats -- often without knowing where they will rebuild next.
Bangladesh has built specific institutions and programs for other fragile geographies. In 2000, it established the Bangladesh Haor and Wetland Development Board, followed by a 20-year Haor Master Plan in 2012.
The Chittagong Hill Tracts, meanwhile, have a distinctive legal and institutional framework rooted in the 1900 Regulation, the 1997 Peace Accord, and the 1998 Regional Council Act.
Photo: Courtesy
The chars are different. Bangladesh does have programs such as the Char Development and Settlement Project, which has worked on infrastructure, livelihoods and land settlement in newly accreted chars.
But there is still no dedicated statutory framework for a basic reality that erosion-prone char communities face repeatedly: The land can physically disappear, communities can be displaced, and the administrative identity attached to a place can disappear with it.
Our institutions are largely designed for land that stays put. Registration, schools, health facilities, local government records, and land administration become extraordinarily complicated when the land itself is moving.
When a char disappears, it is not only houses that go with it.
I have seen villages where the school, the madrasa, the tube-well and other community facilities vanished into the river in a single season. It is not several separate disasters. It is one settlement disappearing at once.
I worked with these communities for years and witnessed their repeated displacement firsthand.
The inhabitants of Sidhai Char, under Mollarchar Union, have had to shift their entire settlement more than once -- not just their homes, but also the school and an NGO-run weaving centre that had provided local women with a rare source of income.
An entire ecosystem of livelihoods and community life had to be dismantled and rebuilt because nothing could remain anchored to the land once the river took it away.
In nearby Dewanganj, river erosion has also threatened and swallowed schools and other community infrastructure. But at least some communities manage to move together. Some chars do not offer even that possibility.
I think often of Sirajbeg, a char in Kurigram that no longer exists. The river did not simply erode its edges; it eventually took the whole char.
Photo: Courtesy
There was no single relocation and no common destination. Its people scattered to other chars, upazilas and districts across the north -- and, for families I know personally, as far as Dhaka.
They did not resettle as a community. They dispersed as individuals, each finding their own way to survive.
Ask them where they are from, and they will say Sirajbeg.
But Sirajbeg is no longer on the map in the way it once was.
There may be no functioning local institution tied to the vanished settlement, no surviving school record readily accessible to every family, and no land document that every displaced household can produce to establish what it once owned.
What remains is memory -- and memory alone is rarely enough at a land office or government counter.
A community like Sidhai's can lose its buildings and still retain much of its social fabric because it moves together.
A community like Sirajbeg's can lose both the land and the community itself, leaving people scattered across different places and holding records that may no longer reflect where they came from.
When a char reforms, the community does not simply return. It starts again, often without a single institution responsible for helping it do so.
For years, we have advised char families to keep their NID, birth registration, and land documents together and carry them whenever they move. It is sensible advice.
But imagine a family fleeing a collapsing riverbank at night, with children and livestock to save and perhaps one boat available. Is it realistic to expect them to remember a folder of papers?
Sometimes those papers go into the river too.
And even when documents survive, another question remains: Which institution will recognize the family's connection to the place it has left behind?
For a family whose home, school, and local community infrastructure disappeared together, the challenge is immense.
This is not simply a housing issue. It is a question of legal identity, land rights and access to citizenship and public services.
In December 2025, the International Organization for Migration, working with the government of Bangladesh and development partners, released the country's first comprehensive nationwide estimate of disaster-induced internal displacement.
It estimated that 4,955,527 people were currently internally displaced because of natural disasters. The assessment covered all eight divisions, 64 districts, and thousands of local administrative units. A large share of those displaced had been displaced for years rather than only during a recent emergency.
Bangladesh is not starting from zero. The country adopted a national strategy on disaster- and climate-induced internal displacement in 2015 and a broader National Strategy on Internal Displacement Management in 2021. A National Action Plan for implementing that strategy covers 2022-2042.
Programs such as Ashrayan have also provided housing and rehabilitation to hundreds of thousands of landless and homeless families. The Char Development and Settlement Project has worked for decades to improve livelihoods, infrastructure and land settlement in vulnerable char areas.
But a house is not legal identity, and resettlement is not necessarily a secured land claim.
A family can receive a new roof and still struggle to establish its previous land rights. It can be counted as resettled and still move again when the next erosion event arrives.
Its children may have birth registration and NID records, yet the administrative memory of the community they came from can gradually disappear.
This is the gap we need to address.
The river does not simply take land. It can take the administrative memory of a community.
Photo: Courtesy
As Bangladesh considers its next phase of development and climate-adaptation priorities, it should consider creating a dedicated institutional mechanism for the rights and administrative continuity of char communities.
Such a body would not replace existing char-development programmes. Instead, it could fill the gap between development, land administration, legal protection and internal displacement.
It could maintain digital and physical records of land claims that survive relocation; preserve the original identity of vanished settlements; maintain duplicate civil and community records; provide legal assistance to families contesting land and inheritance claims; coordinate services when communities relocate together; and help trace families when a settlement is dispersed across chars, districts or cities.
Most importantly, it could create a system of portable legal and administrative identity for people whose geography is not portable.
The goal is not simply to move people from one place to another.
It is to ensure that when the river takes their land, it does not also take their rights.
Somewhere in Dhaka today, a family may still call itself the people of Sirajbeg -- a char that exists nowhere except in what they remember.
The chars have no legal memory. It is time Bangladesh gave them one.
Ahmed Toufiqur Rahman is a rotarian and development professional with 24 years of experience. Email: thetoufiqrahman@gmail.com .

item.title: Arsenal ride out Liverpool storm to top Premier League
item.description:
Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz's early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners.
The defending champions were made to suffer after the German's 16th-minute opener but held out for what could be a telling win in their quest to retain the title.
Arsenal climbed three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table.
But with City expected to be hit with a severe points penalty, unless they can overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules, Arsenal dealt a huge blow to their most likely rivals for the title.
"It's been such a long time without this feeling here, that we really needed it," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. "We are extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody has done."
Liverpool produced arguably their best spell of Andoni Iraola's early months in charge with a blistering 30 minutes after conceding, but failed to take their chances as the Spaniard suffered just his second defeat in 14 games since arriving from Bournemouth.
Arteta was stinging in his criticism of the Arsenal side that crashed out to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday in one of the biggest ever League Cup shocks.
The Arsenal boss got the response he desired in a strong start from the champions.
Havertz was one of the biggest culprits for wasting chances in midweek but made amends with a simple finish from Declan Rice's precise low cross.
The early goal lit the touchpaper for a pulsating first 45 minutes as Liverpool roared back.
Iraola and Arteta played together as boys for Basque side Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea.
Arteta's old friend gave his side one of the most uncomfortable afternoons they have experienced in recent seasons as Arsenal's rock-solid defence was left clinging on for half-time.
"I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down," said Iraola. "I loved a lot of moments of the game.
"We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. Arsenal are in the best of the situations but it is just the start of November today."
All of Liverpool's three £100 million-plus ($134 million) forwards started together and there are signs the relationship between Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola is beginning to flourish.
Isak did Arsenal a favour by not going down as he was pulled back by Jurrien Timber when just failing to connect with a wicked delivery from Barcola.
"The Alex one is a clear penalty," added Iraola. "We can all see that he holds the shirt (but) because he doesn't go to the floor, you are not going to call the penalty? I don't understand it."
Wirtz curled a free-kick onto the bar from a narrow angle and Alexis Mac Allister should have buried a header into the goal rather than finding the stand behind David Raya's goal.
Half-time allowed Arsenal the chance to reset and take the wind out of Liverpool's sails as Iraola's men tired in the second period.
Alisson Becker produced a stunning save to turn behind Christos Tzolis's shot that was arrowing into the bottom corner to keep Liverpool in the game.
That intervention counted for little as Arsenal rode out the closing stages to register another clean sheet and an eighth win in nine league games.
Defeat leaves fifth-placed Liverpool nine points adrift of the leaders and already facing a mountain to climb to get back in the title race.

item.title: Bangladesh slip in WTC standings after defeat to West Indies
item.description:
An eight-wicket defeat to West Indies in the opening Test of the two-match series saw Bangladesh slip from fourth to fifth in the World Test Championship (WTC) standings.
Bangladesh started the match with an aim to make a giant leap toward the maiden final appearance in the WTC. But the outside chance of making it final received a massive setback after the defeat, which allowed India to move up to fourth.
Bangladesh's points percentage fell from 55.56 to 47.62 while India currently stands at 51.52 per cent.
The West Indies, meanwhile, improved their points percentage from 20.83 to 26.92 following their victory, although they remain eighth in the table.
They have narrowed the gap on seventh-placed Sri Lanka, who have a points percentage of 33.33.
Chasing a target of 170, the West Indies reached 172-2 in just 35.1 overs on Day 4, frequently interrupted by rain, lightening and bad light.
Brandon King led the run-chase with 81 not out while his fellow opener John Campbell made 49. Kevam Hodge was unbeaten on 31 with King when West Indies sealed the deal with incredible ease.
West Indies captain Roston Chase said the team was targeting an improvement in their position in the WTC standings, a goal achieved showing a superlative performance. "We came here with the aim of improving our rankings by winning two Tests. We want to finish the cycle at least at number six or five on the points table. To achieve that goal, we had to win both these matches," Chase said after the match.
Earlier, Bangladesh were bowled out for 272 in their first innings, with opener Shadman Islam scoring 105. West Indies left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican claimed five wickets.
In reply, the visitors were wrapped up for 245 in the first innings, with John Campbell and Tagenarine Chanderpaul making half-centuries. Justin Greaves scored 46, while Chase added 43. Nayeem Hasan was Bangladesh's leading bowler with 4-33.
A sensational batting collapse saw Bangladesh dismissed for 142 in the second innings, leaving West Indies a modest 170 for victory. Chase was the wrecker-in-chief with 5-33 while Warrican added 4-63 with his five-wicket haul in the first innings.
The West Indies completed the chase comfortably, securing a victory that boosted their WTC campaign and further reshaped the points standings.
Meanwhile, Australia slipped from first to third in the standings following a 176-run defeat to South Africa in Cape Town, while New Zealand climbed to the top of the table.
South Africa moved into second place after the victory, with their points percentage rising to 71.43 from 66.67. New Zealand now lead the standings with 72.22 per cent, while Australia's percentage dropped to 69.23.
Australia, chasing a target of 288 on the final day of the third Test, were bowled out for just 111 before the end of the second session, handing South Africa a comprehensive victory.

item.title: Amite replaces Mominul for final West Indies Test
item.description:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has called up Amite Hasan to their 15-member squad for the second and final Test against the West Indies, replacing the injured Mominul Haque.
The BCB announced the squad in a press release on Saturday, confirming one change from the opening Test which Bangladesh lost by eight wickets after a sensational batting debacle at Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium.
Mominul sustained a head injury on the third day of the first Test while fielding at short leg. He was injured while attempting to take a catch in the 78th over of the West Indies' first innings, with Jaker Ali Anik subsequently coming in as his concussion substitute.
According to the BCB, players who suffer a concussion must remain out of action for at least seven days before returning to the field. As a result, Mominul will miss the second Test, paving the way for Amite's inclusion.
"The concussion rule that states that a player diagnosed with a concussion must observe a mandatory minimum of seven calendar days away from play before returning to the field," the BCB press release stated.
Meanwhile, Jaker Ali has retained his place in the 15-member squad after featuring as Mominul's concussion replacement in the first Test.
The second and final Test of the series is scheduled to begin on November 5 at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium.

item.title: Democrats, Trump hold final rallies before midterm elections
item.description:
US-CALIFORNIA-HOUSE-CANDIDATE-RANDY-VILLEGAS-CAMPAIGNS-AHEAD-OF

Donald Trump and his Republican Party will make last-gasp pitches to US midterm voters Monday to hold back a predicted Democrat wave that could take over Congress and impose tight political constraints on the president for the first time in two years.

For his closing argument, Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool -- a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old president's obsessive, controversial drive to redevelop the US capital.

"We're going to win," he said on Sunday.

Democrats, meanwhile, began making their final arguments, planning rallies -- including by star Democratic Senate candidates James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas -- to cap a campaign of breathtaking tension and bitterness.

Polls are largely in their favor, showing that Democrats are near certain to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives and have a real shot at winning the currently Republican Senate.

Even winning just the House would mean Democrats have voting power over the federal budget and would lead powerful committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues.

The loss of total Republican dominance would push Trump into unfamiliar territory: a lame-duck period beset with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington.

But a decade into the Trump era, Democrats are wary about predictions of victory.

"Nauseously optimistic," Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood.

Scorched earth

Democrats are also facing late internal divisions, with left-wing candidates clashing at times with the party's establishment.

In a startling display of infighting on Sunday, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens in Michigan endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers against left-wing progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed in her state's key Senate race.

Trump was quick to praise Stevens for her "bravery", posting on his Truth Social platform that "Haley said what few people are willing to say."

Stevens, who lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite being backed by the Democratic establishment, struggled to explain her decision in an interview with CNN.

"It's just where I was at the end of the night and earlier this morning," she said.

Trump's Republicans have fought a political scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and openly branding El-Sayed, who is Muslim, as a terrorist.

Addressing a crowd in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said Democrats are "extreme and dangerous radicals" who will "steal your wealth" and let in migrants to "ransack, rape and plunder."

But polls show Americans souring on Trump''s wrecking-ball act.

An NBC News poll released on Sunday showed 60 per cent disapprove of his performance, particularly over high prices exacerbated by his now eight-month-long war against Iran.

While the House seems highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is up in the air.

The final New York Times/Siena poll released Sunday evening showed Democratic candidates leading in all seven seats viewed as most competitive, though five remained within the margin of error.

Only a third of the Senate's 100 seats are being contested in these midterms, and few of the races were seen as favorable to Democrats.

However, with surprisingly strong challenges in deeply Republican states, pollsters now say the odds of a Democratic flip are at minimum even.

The final New York Times/Siena poll released Sunday evening showed Democratic candidates leading in all seven seats viewed as most competitive, though five remained within the margin of error.

A Democratic Senate would be able to shut down Trump's lifetime appointments to courts -- including the Supreme Court.

While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country.

The midterms have seen about USD 11 billion spent on advertising, with large chunks coming from individual mega-donors.

Elon Musk, a close Trump ally who led the so-called DOGE effort in dismantling entire government departments, has given a staggering nearly half-billion dollars to help get Republicans elected.

item.title: Garment workers continue protests demanding Tk30,000 minimum wage
item.description:
Garment workers again staged protests and blocked roads across industrial areas in Gazipur, Savar-Ashulia and Narayanganj on Monday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, an end to worker blacklisting and a halt to layoffs.
The demonstrations triggered clashes with law enforcement agencies, vandalism and arson, leaving at least 10 people, including a Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) member, police personnel, journalists and BNP activists, injured. At least 264 factories in Savar and Ashulia declared general holidays amid fears of further unrest.
In Gazipur, thousands of workers gathered at Palli Bidyut in Safipur and Chandra intersection in Kaliakair early in the morning, blocking the Dhaka-Tangail highway and bringing traffic to a standstill.
The blockade began around 8:30am, with workers from several factories occupying the highway. Police and BGB personnel later moved to clear the road, initially attempting to persuade the protesters to leave.
However, the situation turned violent when a section of workers hurled brickbats at law enforcers, seriously injuring a BGB member. Police fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the protesters.
Around noon, further clashes broke out in the Naojor area of Gazipur city, where protesters vandalised several police vehicles and set one on fire. Three journalists covering the incidents were also injured, while a camera belonging to Somoy TV was vandalised.
The journalists were Mehedi Hasan, Gazipur correspondent of Somoy TV, his cameraman, Reza Islam, a cameraman of SA TV, and Ifthekhar Raihan of Ekhon TV.
The blockade severely disrupted traffic along the Dhaka-Tangail highway, a key economic corridor connecting Dhaka with northern Bangladesh. After nearly five hours, traffic gradually returned to normal through the intervention of law enforcement agencies.
Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Amzad Hossain said more than 150 factories had declared general holidays to prevent further unrest.
He said district police, metropolitan police, industrial police and BGB personnel were jointly working to restore order, adding that the situation had gradually started to calm down.
Kaliakair Upazila Nirbahi Officer AHM Fakhrul Hossain said the administration was taking workers' demands seriously and coordinating with the relevant authorities to address their grievances. He urged all concerned to remain peaceful.
In Savar and Ashulia, workers took to the streets for the third consecutive day, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, an end to blacklisting and a halt to layoffs.
Protests spread across several locations, including Baroipara, Nischintapur, Baipail, Jirabo, Kathgara, Ghoshbag and Narsinghpur, disrupting factory operations and triggering repeated confrontations with police.
Workers at Newage Garments in Nischintapur stopped work and later gathered outside nearby factories. Demonstrations also broke out near Bengal Plastic Pipes Ltd on the Jirabo-Kathgara road and along the Abdullahpur-Baipail road.
Around 1pm, clashes erupted in Narsinghpur when police attempted to disperse workers staging a sit-in. Protesters hurled bricks and stones, prompting police to fire tear gas shells. The unrest also saw a covered van set on fire, while a police officer was injured in a separate clash near a Ha-Meem Group factory.
Police detained two people during the incidents.
Superintendent of Police of Industrial Police-1 Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan confirmed that 264 factories across the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt had declared general holidays.
He said additional police personnel had been deployed to prevent further incidents, adding that workers had left their workplaces amid the unrest and that operations at several factories had been suspended.
Meanwhile, garment workers blocked the Dhaka-Narayanganj Link Road in the Shibu Market area of Fatullah around 12:30pm, bringing traffic to a halt and leaving commuters stranded.
Thousands of workers from several factories, including Metro Knitting, Palmal Garments, Abir Fashion, Azad-Rifat Dyeing, Liberty and Midland, joined the demonstration, carrying sticks and chanting slogans.
Alongside the Tk30,000 minimum wage demand, the protesters called for an end to attacks on garment workers.
Md Shahin Ahmed, president of the district unit of the Garment Workers Trade Union, said the demonstration began in Shibu Market and later spread across several kilometres.
He said resentment over police attacks on garment workers in different parts of Dhaka had also contributed to the protests in Narayanganj, although workers there had remained largely peaceful in recent days.
Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Operations) Tarek Al Mehedi said police had been deployed to the area after receiving reports of the blockade and were trying to resolve the situation through discussions with workers.
On Sunday, garment workers also staged protests in Konabari, Safipur, Palli Bidyut and surrounding industrial areas in Gazipur, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Intermittent clashes with police, vandalism and arson were reported, including the torching of a police box and damage to several vehicles. The unrest disrupted traffic on the Dhaka-Tangail highway for around six hours. Several journalists covering the demonstrations in the Chandra area were also reportedly assaulted, with their mobile phones snatched.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir joins Commonwealth FMs’ meeting ahead of CHOGM 2026
item.description:
Acting Foreign Minister Humaiun Kobir on Monday joined the Foreign Ministers and Heads of Delegation of Commonwealth nations to discuss progress made by different Commonwealth bodies and forums and provide guidance on the organisation's future action plans.
He led the Bangladesh delegation to the opening session of the pre-CHOGM Commonwealth Foreign Affairs Ministers' Meeting at the American University of Antigua in St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda.
On Sunday evening, the acting foreign minister arrived in St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda, to lead the Bangladesh delegation to the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), which has the theme "Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth".
He is expected to make interventions at the high-level executive session of the Foreign Ministers' Meeting and the Heads of Government-level meeting.
On the sidelines, the Acting Foreign Minister will hold a series of bilateral meetings, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Indian External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar is leading the Indian delegation to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, but it could not be confirmed whether the two ministers would meet on the sidelines of the CHOGM.
This year's meeting is being held under the theme "Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth".
The event is focusing on strengthening partnerships among member countries, promoting sustainable investment and addressing shared challenges, including climate resilience, trade, innovation and sustainable development.
The Commonwealth comprises 56 member countries across Africa, Asia, the Caribbean, the Americas, Europe and the Pacific.
The Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, known as CHOGM, is the Commonwealth's principal forum for dialogue and collective decision-making. Since the first meeting in 1971, it has brought leaders together as equal partners to address shared challenges and advance cooperation across diverse regions and economies.
Kobir's broader engagements at the CHOGM are expected to provide opportunities for Bangladesh to strengthen diplomatic relations and discuss issues of mutual interest with Commonwealth partners, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday.
The CHOGM is a biennial summit bringing together heads of government, ministers and representatives from business, civil society and youth organisations, a senior official said, noting that the event marks a significant occasion for the Caribbean nation.
He will attend the opening and executive sessions of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), as well as several foreign minister-level meetings and a number of bilateral meetings with ministers from other countries.

item.title: LPG price hiked again, 12kg cylinder now Tk2,060
item.description:
The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has raised liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices by Tk223 per 12kg cylinder, setting the new price at Tk2,060 amid an ongoing supply shortage.
The price was previously Tk1,837. The price of autogas has also increased from Tk84.62 to Tk91.95 per litre.
The revised prices will take effect at 8:00pm on Monday, BERC said.
Prices have been raised across all cylinder sizes, ranging from 5kg to 45kg.
BERC last raised the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder by Tk252 on October 4, from Tk1,585 to Tk1,837. The latest hike comes just a month later, amid ongoing supply shortages and complaints of higher market prices.
On October 29, BERC held a public hearing on LPG prices and proposed increases in storage, bottling and distribution charges. During the hearing, LPG operators, distributors and retailers placed separate proposals for raising their charges.
Operators proposed increasing bottling charges from Tk15–16 to Tk25–30 per kg. They also sought to raise distribution charges from Tk4.17 to Tk8.33 per kg and retail charges from Tk3.75 to Tk10 per kg.
Distributors proposed increasing their charge on each 12kg cylinder from Tk50 to Tk150, while retailers sought to raise theirs from Tk45 to Tk70.
After reviewing the proposals, BERC's technical evaluation committee recommended raising the price of a 12kg cylinder from Tk1,837 to Tk1,976, an increase of Tk139.
Following the hearing, the commission set November 2 as the deadline for submitting opinions on the proposals. It announced the revised prices on the final day for receiving feedback.

item.title: Garment worker protests disrupt operations at 264 factories in Savar, Ashulia
item.description:
At least 264 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia declared general holidays on Monday following clashes between workers and police over demands for a minimum wage increase and other labor-related issues.
Superintendent of Police of Industrial Police-1 Mominul Islam Bhuiyan confirmed the development on Monday afternoon.
For the 3rd consecutive day, garment workers in the industrial areas of Savar and Ashulia took to the streets demanding a Tk30,000 increase in the minimum wage, an end to blacklisting and a halt to worker layoffs.
In the morning, workers blocked the Nabinagar-Chandra Road in the Baroipara area, pressing for the wage increase and 3 other demands. Police later persuaded them to leave the road.
Meanwhile, workers at Newage Garments in the Nischintapur area entered the factory premises and staged a work stoppage. They later gathered in front of Ananta Garments on the Baipail-Abdullahpur Road.
Several factories, including Knit Asia, Al-Muslim, Trouser Line and Ananta Garments, declared general holidays on Monday, as they had on the previous day.
Later, when workers staged a sit-in on the road, police attempted to disperse them. At one point, workers threw bricks and stones at police, triggering clashes and chases between the two sides.
Police fired tear gas shells to disperse the protesters. During the unrest, agitated workers also set fire to a covered van in the Narsinghpur area, further escalating tensions in the industrial zone.
According to police, incidents of brick-throwing and subsequent clashes were reported in front of the factories of Picard Bangladesh Ltd, Artistic Design, Janoron Sweater Ltd, Ferrari Garments Ltd, Denitex Limited, Anlima Textile Limited, Al Islam Textile Limited and GQ Industries.
Police later attempted to bring the situation under control through discussions with workers. Two garment workers were detained during the incidents.
Mominul Islam Bhuiyan said the unrest in the Savar industrial area stemmed from workers' demands.
He said general holidays had been declared at 264 garment factories across the Savar-Ashulia industrial area due to the unrest. Additional police personnel were also deployed in the area to prevent further incidents.

item.title: 10,500 sued in four cases filed over Mirpur workers’ clashes, arson
item.description:
Four cases have been filed over two consecutive days of workers’ protests, clashes, arson and attacks on police in Mirpur, Dhaka.
The cases name about 10,500 unidentified people as accused. So far, 22 people have been arrested. The Detective Branch (DB) of police claims that 11 of them are activists of the Awami League, whose activities have been banned, Jubo League, and Chhatra League.
Law enforcement operations continue in connection with the violence surrounding the workers’ movement demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Officers-in-charge (OCs) of Mirpur Model and Pallabi police stations shared the information on Monday afternoon.
Md Hafizur Rahman, OC of Mirpur Model Police Station, said one case has been filed over vandalism of a traffic box and attacks on police in Mirpur. Three thousand unidentified people have been named as accused in the case. Six people have been arrested so far.
Meanwhile, Jalal Uddin, OC of Pallabi Police Station, said three cases have been filed at Pallabi over arson on a police vehicle, attacks on police, obstruction of government duties, and vandalism of a traffic box. Police are the complainants in these cases.
He said each case names between 2,000 and 2,500 unidentified people as accused. So far, 16 people have been arrested in the three cases.
The DB says local activists of the Awami League had planned to create violence in Mirpur by exploiting the workers’ movement for their just demands. A section of them had organised through online groups. They also had plans for large-scale sabotage under the cover of the movement.
Of those detained in Mirpur, 11 are activists of the Awami League, Jubo League and Chhatra League. They are not local garment workers. According to the DB’s claim, they came from various districts and gathered in Mirpur.
Meanwhile, at around 10:45am on Monday, workers tried to take to the road through an alley in the Senpara Parbata area of Mirpur-10. Police dispersed them and also fired several tear gas shells.
Later, workers also tried to take to the road at Proshika Intersection beside the Mirpur-2 Stadium. Police moved them away from there as well.
Eyewitnesses said workers were coming in scattered groups from the Rupnagar area, passing by the Mirpur-2 Stadium towards Proshika Intersection. When they tried to get onto the road, police obstructed them at around 11am. Tension arose between police and workers.
After two consecutive days of garment workers’ protests and clashes in Mirpur, police and other law enforcement personnel have been on alert since Monday morning. Police were seen stationed at the Mirpur-10 roundabout and surrounding areas from the morning. Riot-control vehicles, water cannons and other vehicles have been kept ready at the roundabout.
However, traffic on the roads at Mirpur-10 and surrounding areas is normal on Monday. No disruption was seen on the roads.
On Monday morning, after a meeting at the secretariat with representatives of owners on the recent situation in the garment industry, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, responding to journalists’ questions, said some industrialists and a few individuals operating under the banner of workers’ organisations are involved in creating unrest in the garment sector. Video footage, audio and other evidence of these individuals’ activities have been collected. Some people were brought under the law on Sunday as well.
He said strict action would be taken if anyone tried to worsen the law and order situation in the name of the workers’ movement.
On Sunday, garment factory workers blocked the road and demonstrated at the Mirpur-10 intersection in the capital, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Around 8am that day, workers from several garment factories took position on the road, disrupting traffic in the surrounding areas.
Clashes between workers and police began at around 11:15am. According to eyewitnesses, police used batons, water cannons, sound grenades and tear gas shells to disperse the workers. The workers then also hurled bricks and stones at police from various directions.
Chases and counter-chases between the two sides continued until 11:45am. At one point around midday, a police vehicle was set on fire beneath the Mirpur-11 metro station.
Because of the clashes, the Mirpur-10, Mirpur-11 and Pallabi metro stations were closed from 11:38am to 1:58pm.
The day before, on Saturday, garment workers had also blocked roads in Mirpur over the same demand. That day, from 10:30am to 1pm, traffic came to a standstill in Mirpur-10, 11 and 12 and surrounding areas.

item.title: COP31: Bangladesh to highlight climate resilience, seek grants
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Monday said Bangladesh will urge developed countries to provide climate finance in the form of grants rather than loans and take responsibility for their contribution to global carbon emissions at the upcoming COP31, scheduled to be held in Antalya, Turkey, from November 9 to 20.
Talking to reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, she said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would make a brief visit to attend the two-day high-level sessions of the conference.
COP is the annual UN Climate Summit, officially known as the Conference of the Parties.
The prime minister will participate in the World Leaders’ Summit, scheduled for November 11-12, a senior official told UNB.
“The prime minister's visit will be formally announced at a press conference, as we do ahead of every foreign visit. You will know the details then,” Shama said.
She said Bangladesh would highlight its achievements in climate resilience and its experience in addressing the impacts of climate change across South Asia and the wider Asian region.
At the same time, Bangladesh would highlight the support it needs to tackle future climate challenges, particularly the need to ensure that climate finance is provided as grants rather than loans, she said.
The state minister stressed the need for major carbon-emitting countries to take responsibility and ensure accountability during climate negotiations.
“Although Bangladesh's contribution to global carbon emissions is almost negligible, we are ultimately among those suffering the consequences,” she said.
Shama said the government would also showcase the initiatives taken by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman over the past six months to address climate change and improve the environment.
These include canal excavation, tree plantation drives, and greater emphasis on solar power and renewable energy, which directly contribute to tackling climate change, she said.
An inter-ministerial coordination meeting chaired by State Minister Shama was held last month to review Bangladesh's preparations for the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31).
The meeting reviewed various aspects of the preparations, including the Prime Minister's participation in the high-level segment of COP31.
Bangladesh's priorities and concerns at COP31 were discussed at the meeting, which also reviewed possible bilateral meetings and seminars to be held on the sidelines at Bangladesh's pavilions in the Blue and Green Zones, an official told UNB.
Asked about the latest developments regarding execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia, Shama said the Bangladesh mission in the Kingdom has been maintaining regular communication with the relevant authorities.
“Communication with Saudi Arabia through our mission is continuing. We hope to receive some information from them soon. The process is underway. We hope to hear something from the Saudi government shortly,” she said.

item.title: Experts call for subsidies to promote organic fertilizers
item.description:
Experts and policymakers have called for government subsidies to promote the production and use of organic fertilizers, citing concerns over declining soil fertility, food nutrition and the sustainability of agriculture in Bangladesh.
Despite achieving self-sufficiency in food production, Bangladesh continues to face nutritional challenges, ranking 84th among 122 countries in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2026. Meanwhile, prolonged dependence on chemical fertilizers has contributed to declining soil fertility, raising concerns about the long-term sustainability of agricultural production.
The call was made at a roundtable titled “Subsidizing and Promoting Organic Fertilizer for Healthy Soil, Crops and Environment” at the CIRDAP Auditorium in Dhaka on Monday.
ActionAid Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute (BARI), in collaboration with 20 national and international development organizations and 5 universities, jointly organized the event.
Agricultural experts, government officials, development organizations, farmers and organic fertilizer entrepreneurs discussed barriers to production, registration, marketing and use, along with ways to facilitate access to government subsidies.
Speakers highlighted administrative complications in registering organic fertilizer products and gaps in quality assessment and monitoring mechanisms. While acknowledging that organic fertilizers may produce lower yields than chemical alternatives in some cases, they stressed their importance in maintaining soil health and improving crop quality.
They also called for balanced fertilizer use based on soil conditions and crop requirements.
Dr Md Abdus Salam, executive chairman of the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council (BARC), attended the first technical session as the chief guest. He discussed the existing registration process for entrepreneurs and invited recommendations to simplify it.
Mosammat Sabira Sultana, MP and member of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Agriculture, attended the event as a special guest.
“Just as keeping a mother healthy help ensure the birth of a healthy child, maintaining soil health makes it possible to produce nutritious crops,” she said.
She stressed the importance of quality assurance, effective marketing and identifying genuine farmers under the Farmer Card initiative.
Sultana urged participants to prepare specific proposals and an action plan for the balanced use of organic and chemical fertilizers. She pledged to raise the recommendations with the parliamentary standing committee, parliament and the prime minister.
Anwar Faruque, director of Bangladesh Krishi Bank, attended the second technical session as the chief guest and proposed introducing a district-level registration system for organic fertilizer entrepreneurs.
“There is no alternative to natural methods if we are to make agriculture sustainable,” he said, emphasizing balanced fertilizer use and the need to provide farmers with accurate, science-based information.
Farah Kabir, country director of ActionAid Bangladesh, called for coordinated efforts to strengthen quality control, address marketing irregularities and reduce administrative barriers. She also expressed the organization's willingness to work with the government on necessary policy reforms.
The second session was chaired by Professor Dr Abdul Karim of the International University of Business, Agriculture and Technology (IUBAT).
Dr M Nazim Uddin of BARI and Professor Dr Md Mizanur Rahman of Gazipur Agricultural University presented research papers during the 2 sessions.
The discussions are expected to inform the development of a policy framework for subsidies, simpler registration procedures and stronger quality assurance mechanisms for organic fertilizers.

item.title: Traffic fines can now be paid easily thru bKash app, agent points
item.description:
Traffic fines can now be paid instantly through the bKash app in just a few taps, without any hassle.
It can also be paid from more than 350,000 bKash agent points across the country.
The service, launched jointly by Community Bank and bKash, allows users to clear fines for all types of traffic cases filed by the Bangladesh Police.
Whenever needed, customers can instantly pay traffic fines from anywhere in the country using the ‘Pay Bill’ option from the home screen in the bKash app.
They can also avail instant traffic fine payment services from any nearby bKash agent points.
The service aims to enable on-the-spot settlement whenever a case is filed for violating traffic rules.
After receiving the traffic fine slip, customers can pay the fine anytime and from anywhere using the bKash app.
Alongside, they get the opportunity to quickly retrieve seized documents from the concerned law enforcement officer by showing the payment receipt.
How to pay traffic fines through bKash app
To use this service, a customer needs to tap the ‘Pay Bill’ icon on the home screen of the bKash app.
The ‘Traffic Fine’ feature can be found under the ‘Government Fee’ option or by typing into the search bar.
Next, entering the specific case number written on the traffic case slip will automatically show the fine amount on the screen.
After checking all details, the customer confirms the transaction by entering their PIN, and the fine is cleared instantly.
Upon successful payment, a confirmation SMS and in-app notification will be sent to the customer’s mobile number.
A fee is applicable.
After completing the payment, downloading the digital receipt enables swift recovery of seized documents.
Details regarding this traffic fine payment feature are available at: https://tinyurl.com/4udymf5p .
To pay traffic fines at nearby agent points, customers need to provide the case ID and their mobile number to the agent.
Once the fine is settled, the customer will receive a digital receipt directly from the agent.

item.title: BB, IFIC Bank join Tk2,000cr pre-financing fund for export-oriented frozen food sector
item.description:
IFIC Bank PLC and Bangladesh Bank have signed an agreement for IFIC Bank’s participation in the Tk2,000 crore pre-financing fund established by Bangladesh Bank to facilitate financing for the export-oriented frozen food sector.
The agreement was signed on Sunday, November 1, at a ceremony held at Bangladesh Bank’s head office.
The ceremony was presided over by AKM Sayduzzaman, director of Agricultural Credit Department-2, Bangladesh Bank.
Arief Hossain Khan, executive director of Bangladesh Bank, attended the ceremony as chief guest.
Representing IFIC Bank were Helal Ahmed, chief of branch business, and Fariha Haider, head of SME & retail banking (current charge).
The fund has been established by Bangladesh Bank to provide necessary financing facilities to engaged in the export-oriented frozen food sector.
The initiative aims to enhance production and export capacity, facilitate the expansion of export activities, and contribute to the country's overall economic development.
Through its extensive nationwide network of branches and sub-branches, IFIC Bank continues to provide essential banking and financing facilities to customers across the country.
Participation in Bangladesh Bank's pre-financing fund will further expand the Bank's financing support for the export-oriented frozen food sector and strengthen IFIC Bank's contribution to export growth and sustainable economic development in Bangladesh.

item.title: CAL to acquire 51% stake in Hong-Kong based fund manager Asia Frontier Capital
item.description:
Capital Alliance Holdings PLC (CAL), the parent company of CAL Bangladesh, has signed an agreement through its wholly owned Singapore-based subsidiary, CAL Global Pte. Ltd., to acquire a 51% stake in Hong Kong-based fund manager Asia Frontier Capital Ltd. (AFC).
The proposed transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals, including clearance from the Securities and Futures Commission of Hong Kong.
The acquisition marks a major milestone in CAL's international expansion, linking its existing operations in Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and Singapore with AFC’s investment platform in Hong Kong and its on-the-ground teams in Vietnam, Uzbekistan, and Iraq.
Founded in 2013 by Thomas Hugger, AFC manages approximately USD 125 million in assets under management (AUM) for investors across North America, Europe, and Asia.
Its portfolio features the multi-country AFC Asia Frontier Fund as well as dedicated funds for Vietnam, Iraq, and Uzbekistan.
AFC has also maintained a long-standing investment footprint in Sri Lankan and Bangladeshi equities.
Kanishke Mannakkara, group CEO of CAL, said the partnership establishes a vital conduit to connect international capital with high-growth frontier markets.
"Frontier markets offer some of the most compelling growth stories in the world, yet they remain hard for international investors to reach," Mannakkara said.
"This partnership changes that... Together with AFC, we will serve as a conduit for international capital to access frontier markets and, just as importantly, for investors in our markets to access opportunities across the frontier and beyond."
Following the acquisition, Thomas Hugger will remain as founder and CEO of AFC, ensuring continuity in the firm's investment process and team.
"Our investors will continue to benefit from the same approach to managing their money, with the same team, investment process and independence in our decisions," Hugger said.
"What changes is the strength of the platform behind us."
Established in 2000 and listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange, CAL manages over $1.2 billion in assets across Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.
In Bangladesh, CAL operates through CAL Securities Limited—a stockbroker ranking among the top 10% of market participants—and CAL Investments Limited, a merchant bank specializing in mergers and acquisitions advisory and wealth management.
Upon completion of the transaction, CAL and AFC intend to explore expanding AFC's product offerings to include frontier fixed income and country-specific strategies, pending regulatory approval.

item.title: Bank Asia holds Senior management awareness session on RBS framework
item.description:
Bank Asia PLC organized a Senior Management Awareness Session on the newly introduced Risk-Based Supervision (RBS) Framework, in compliance with Bangladesh Bank's regulatory requirements for enhancing awareness among banks' senior management.
The session was conducted by Mohammad Abdur Rab, director, Supervisory Policy and Coordination Department (SPCD), Bangladesh Bank, and Proshanto Kumar Mondol, additional director, SPCD, Bangladesh Bank.
Sohail RK Hussain, managing director of Bank Asia PLC, attended the session along with the bank's senior management team and relevant functional heads, held on October 31 at Bank Asia Tower, Karwan Bazar, Dhaka.
The session focused on the RBS Framework's assessment methodology, supervisory expectations and implementation requirements.
It provided valuable insights into the transition towards a risk-based supervisory approach and enhanced the participants' understanding of the regulatory framework, its implications and the Bank's preparedness for effective implementation.
This initiative reflects Bank Asia’s commitment to further strengthening its corporate governance, risk management and regulatory compliance practices while aligning its operations with Bangladesh Bank’s evolving supervisory framework.

item.title: Prime Bank, Jagannath University ink MoU
item.description:
Prime Bank PLC recently has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Jagannath University to expand banking services for the university’s students, teachers and employees and to promote financial inclusion on campus.
Under the agreement, the university community will have access to Prime Bank’s banking products, card facilities and tailored financial services, while the bank will also support the institution’s own financial needs.
Syed Sazzad Haider Chowdhury, deputy managing director and chief information officer; Shaila Abedin, senior executive vice-president and head of liability and women banking; and MM Mahbub Hasan, senior vice-president and head of financial inclusion and school banking, represented Prime Bank at the signing ceremony.
The Jagannath University delegation was led by vice chancellor Prof Md Rais Uddin and included treasurer Prof Sabina Sharmin, registrar (in-charge) Prof Md Sheikh Gias Uddin, faculty deans, representatives of the Teachers’ Association, and the director of the Office of Finance and Accounts.
Prime Bank officials highlighted a range of financial services for university students, including fee collection, student files, and bank accounts with free debit cards at attractive rates.
They also showcased payroll banking, various loan facilities, credit cards, investment opportunities, and other financial services for faculty members and university staff.
The partnership has been formed under PrimeAcademia, the bank’s industry-academia partnership platform, through which Prime Bank is strengthening its engagement with educational institutions across the country by implementing various innovative banking initiatives.

item.title: Shaila Banu Jhumur joins Southeast Bank board as nominee director
item.description:
Shaila Banu Jhumur joined the board of directors of Southeast Bank PLC. on October 29, as a nominee director representing Welldone Apparel Limited.
Born in Comilla, Shaila Banu Jhumur completed her MSS degree in Political Science from University of Dhaka.
Jhumur is a distinguished entrepreneur, industrialist, and seasoned corporate leader with over 30 years of robust experience spanning global trade and group enterprise management.
Currently, she serves as chairperson of Welldone Apparel Limited (a sister concern of MNR Group), a prominent group operating 100% export-oriented readymade sweater industries.
She seamlessly integrates her extensive background with decades of macroeconomic expertise in managing large-scale industrial operations.
Leveraging global perspectives gained from extensive international travel across numerous countries, she brings a well-rounded worldview to her governance roles.
As an active civic leader, she served as the president of the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) at International School Dhaka (ISD) for two years.
Furthermore, Jhumur is deeply integrated into prominent social and professional networks, maintaining active memberships in elite institutions such as Banani Club Ltd., Dhaka Boat Club Ltd., Uttara Club Ltd., Purbachal Ladies Club Ltd., Gulshan Society, and the Gulshan Joggers Society.

item.title: Crude bomb explodes beneath Agargaon metro station
item.description:
A crude bomb exploded beneath the Agargaon metro rail station in the capital on Monday night.
Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Monirul Islam told Dhaka Tribune that police rushed to the scene after receiving reports of the explosion shortly after 8:30pm.
“Upon reaching the spot, we found that miscreants had detonated a cocktail bomb and fled,” he said.
He added that police were examining CCTV footage from nearby areas to identify those responsible for the explosion.

item.title: Bangladesh, UK express satisfaction over bilateral ties as Kobir meets Miliband
item.description:
Acting Foreign Minister Humaiun Kobir met with UK Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs Ed Miliband on Monday on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in St John's, Antigua and Barbuda.
During the meeting, both ministers expressed satisfaction over the growing bilateral relations between Bangladesh and the UK, marked by robust exports of Bangladeshi goods to the UK market and British investment in Bangladesh.
They also discussed Bangladesh's agreement to purchase Airbus aircraft for its national flag carrier, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The two ministers agreed to extend reciprocal support in multilateral forums on various issues, including climate change, safe, orderly and regular migration, and humanitarian assistance.
The UK Foreign Secretary thanked Bangladesh for hosting around one million forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals (FDMNs) and assured continued British humanitarian support for the Rohingyas.
During the meeting, the Acting Foreign Minister also conveyed an invitation from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to his British counterpart to visit Bangladesh at a mutually convenient time.

item.title: Gazipur labour unrest: 3 cases filed, 30 arrested, 4,000 accused
item.description:
Police have filed three cases over attacks, vandalism and arson during garment workers' protests in Gazipur demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, naming around 4,000 people as accused. At least 30 people have been arrested in connection with the cases.
Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Mohammad Amzad Hossain disclosed the information on Monday afternoon.
Of the three cases, two were filed by the Industrial Police and one by Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP).
Amzad said workers from several garment factories took to the streets on Monday morning in Safipur, Chandra and Palli Bidyut in Kaliakair, as well as Bhogra Bypass, Konabari and Salna in Gazipur city, demanding higher wages.
During the demonstrations, protesters set fire to a police vehicle and blocked highways. Police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel rushed to the areas and fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the protesters and clear the roads.
Clashes and chases and counter-chases subsequently broke out between workers and law enforcers. At one point, a police box in Konabari and several locations, including Palli Bidyut, were set on fire, while several vehicles were vandalised.
Meanwhile, workers' protests had spread across Konabari, Kashimpur, Mouchak, Safipur, Chandra and Palli Bidyut from Sunday morning.
The protesters blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway, bringing traffic to a standstill. The unrest over the past few days has virtually paralysed both the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways, causing severe suffering for passengers travelling to Gazipur and Dhaka from different parts of the country.

item.title: Rafi's record haul fuels dream of direct Olympic qualification
item.description:
Bangladesh Navy swimmer Samiul Islam Rafi once again demonstrated his dominance in the pool, emerging as the standout performer with 11 gold medals at the recently concluded 35th National Swimming, Diving and Water Polo Championship at the National Swimming Complex in Mirpur.
He also clinched the men's best swimmer award for the fourth consecutive edition, further cementing his position as one of the country's leading swimmers.
The 22-year-old from Rajbari believes his performances have improved after spending the last two years training in Thailand. He is now targeting direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, aiming to further improve his timings to achieve that goal.
“I had the opportunity to participate in the 2024 Paris Olympics through a wild card. But this time, I want to qualify directly for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. It’s my dream to compete in Los Angeles. I know I have to improve my performance further to achieve that goal. I am moving forward with that target, preparing myself through hard work and different plans," Rafi told BSS.
Rafi described competing at the 2024 Paris Olympics as the biggest achievement of his career so far.
"Taking part in the Paris Olympics in 2024 remains the biggest achievement of my career. At that time, I could not dominate in as many events as I do now. Gradually, I am improving. Every athlete dreams of competing at the Olympics, the biggest sporting stage in the world, and representing their country there was a great achievement for me.
“My record in Thailand was another special achievement. I set a South Asian record in the 50-metre backstroke. These achievements really inspire me,” he said.
Rafi established eight new national records at the national meet, including four in individual events — the 50m backstroke, 50m butterfly, 50m freestyle and 100m freestyle.
He also helped set records in four team events — the 4x100m freestyle relay, 4x100m mixed medley relay, 4x100m medley relay and 4x100m mixed freestyle relay. Besides his record-breaking performances, he won gold in the 200m breaststroke, 100m butterfly and 100m breaststroke.
Rafi said his two-year training stint in Thailand had played a significant role in his development. His progress there also earned him an opportunity to train in France.
“I trained in Thailand for the last two years. As my performance improved, I got the opportunity to train in France from Thailand. France has many world-class swimmers. I trained alongside them and learned a lot. I gained valuable knowledge and experience, which I am now able to apply in every moment of my performance,” he said.
Rafi clocked 25.81 seconds to win gold in the 50m backstroke, bettering his previous national record of 26.05 seconds set at the 2025 edition.
The Navy swimmer said the timing had exceeded his expectations.
“The 50 and 100-metre backstroke are my favourite events, and I won gold in both. The timing in the 50-metre backstroke was quite unexpected. I never thought I would achieve such a good time. I was initially surprised by the result, but I was extremely happy. I believe this performance has taken me a long way forward. It shows that I am improving, and that gives me confidence to move ahead with even greater determination,” he said.
Rafi lost his father in a road accident when he was just eight years old. His journey in competitive swimming began in 2016, when he was in Class VII and took part in the talent hunt programme titled 'Search for the Best Swimmer'. He subsequently earned a place in the Bangladesh Swimming Federation's training camp, where his talent was identified.
"I first learned to swim at the age of three in my village. In 2016, through the 'Search for the Best Swimmer' programme, I entered competitive swimming. From the beginning, I dreamed of becoming the country's best swimmer. The Navy is an iconic institution for many swimmers. Inspired by that, I joined the Bangladesh Navy," he said.
Rafi also urged young people to take up swimming, calling on parents to encourage their children to pursue the sport from an early age.
“In our country, many children start swimming at a very young age in villages, mostly for recreation and enjoyment. However, we often start professional swimming much later. In many countries, children take up swimming professionally from an early age, and their parents are very serious about it. They provide their children with encouragement and support.
“I believe that if parents in our country also come forward and encourage their children, we can produce many talented swimmers who will bring glory to the nation," he added.
Rafi is now preparing for the 18th World Aquatics Swimming Championships (25m), scheduled to be held in Beijing, China, in December. He aims not only to improve his personal bests but also to reach the semifinals of the global competition.

item.title: Bangladesh hold China to 1-1 draw in Asian Champions Trophy
item.description:
Bangladesh produced a spirited performance to hold China to a 1-1 draw in their final pool-stage match of the Hero Asian Champions Trophy 2026 at Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Punjab on Monday.
Having suffered defeats in their first four matches against India, Japan, Malaysia and South Korea, Bangladesh bounced back with their best performance of the tournament to earn their first point.
China took an early lead through Chen Benhai, who scored in the second minute. However, Bangladesh fought back and found the equaliser in the third quarter.
The goal came in the 38th minute when captain Ashraful Islam converted a penalty stroke to bring Bangladesh level.
The Bangladesh defence then held firm to deny China a winner and secure a valuable draw.
Despite the result, Bangladesh finished at the bottom of the six-team pool table with one point from five matches, while China ended fifth with two points.

item.title: Ukraine, Russia see emergency alert systems hacked
item.description:
Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit in cyberattacks overnight, with fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes broadcast to users in both countries.
The systems have since been brought back under control, though much remains unclear about the attacks, including who was responsible.
Phone notifications were sent to millions across Ukraine late Sunday warning of a “nuclear alert,” a “chemical threat” and even “street fights” in Kyiv.
One of the messages was in Russian and included a link to a new Telegram account named “Hitcore,” the logo of which is a metallic eagle emblazoned over the Russian tricolor flag.
Ukraine’s air force said the “air alert” app -- which typically warns of incoming Russian drone and missile attacks -- had been “subjected to hostile interference.”
Air force spokesman Yuri Ignat confirmed the hack to AFP.
A few hours later, Russia’s emergency situations ministry said that a “massive cyberattack” had hit its own application, with “false information” sent to the public.
Several regional social media accounts run by the department sent out messages warning of a imminent nuclear attack on Russia.
For instance, a Telegram message was sent by authorities in the Belgorod border region warning “nuclear warheads ... have been launched at all regions of Russia,” and telling people to “urgently stock up on food for three weeks.”
Ukraine’s air alert app is widely used to warn of Russian missile and drone attacks. It has been downloaded more than 46 million times and has more than 6.7 million daily users, according to developers, Ajax Systems.
Made with support from the digital transformation ministry, it uses air force data to send mobile notifications at the same time country-wide sirens and loudspeakers announce the start of an air raid, urging people to seek shelter.
The alerts blare out day and night in almost all regions of the country.
The hack did not affect other alert systems or government-backed apps that deliver drone and missile warnings.
The app developers temporarily disabled notifications before saying Monday that operations had been restored.
Russia does not have a nationwide air alert system, and beyond border regions does not routinely send warnings to citizens of incoming Ukrainian attacks.
Few Russians use the affected application, run by the ministry of emergency situations.
Some regional authorities, which take information from the ministry, appear to have either automatically posted the spoof message, or circulated the information on their social media channels.
It remains unclear if the attacks were part of the war, carried out by either side, or launched by independent actors or groups.
Ukraine’s Centre for Strategic Communication, a government-backed project set up to counter Russian propaganda and online threats, said “Russians have hacked” the app.
Air force spokesman Ignat told Ukrainian TV: “The Russians did indeed attack this app.”
A pro-Russian group calling itself Hitcore claimed responsibility for the hack of the Ukrainian alert system.
The group launched a Telegram channel shortly before the attack and included a link to the page in the first message it sent through the system.
One post on the page, addressed to Ukraine’s SBU security services and written in Russian said: “Your government is losing” and urged Kyiv’s spies to defect.
Nobody has claimed responsibility for the hack of the Russian system.
